title: On 15 October Anthropic made Opus 5.5 fast mode available without a waitlist, Microsoft said it had finished pre-training MAI-Base-2 for Foundry weight licensing, and Anthropic told investors Q3 revenue hit $16.8 billion. OpenAI notified developers that GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 leave the API on 14 January 2027.
summary: On Wednesday 15 October 2026 Anthropic’s Claude Platform release notes said fast mode for Claude Opus 5.5 is out of research preview: no access request and no beta header, with default fast-mode rate limits on the Start, Build and Scale tiers, and availability on Claude in Microsoft Foundry for Azure-hosted deployments. Fast mode uses the same model weights and can reach up to 2.5 times standard output-token throughput at $8 and $40 per million input and output tokens, against $4 and $20 at standard speed. The same day Microsoft AI published that it had completed pre-training MAI-Base-2, a mixture-of-experts model with 80 billion active and 2.8 trillion total parameters, trained on 16,000 GB200 GPUs over 38 days, and said organic training data with no distillation will let it license weights to trusted partners through Foundry. On 14–15 October, people familiar with a pre-IPO investor meeting told CNBC and others that Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, up from about $11.6 billion in the second quarter, said it was profitable on an adjusted basis, and told the Financial Times it generated $1.70 in revenue for every dollar spent on computing. Separately, OpenAI’s deprecations page dated 14 October says GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini, including fine-tunes, leave the API on 14 January 2027, with gpt-6-luna as the recommended replacement — about three months’ notice, against the company’s stated six-month minimum for generally available models.
uncertainty: Anthropic’s $16.8 billion figure and profitability claims come from people familiar with a private investor meeting, as reported by CNBC, the Financial Times, Axios, Bloomberg and Reuters. They are not audited public filings, and the November IPO timing remains reported rather than confirmed in a filing. Microsoft’s MAI-Base-2 claims, including FLOPs-efficiency versus DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base, come from Microsoft AI’s own blog; the model is still in post-training and is not a generally available product. Fast mode has separate rate limits and capacity, is not available on Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS or Google Cloud, and does not speed time to first token. OpenAI’s GPT-4o / GPT-4.1 shutdown applies to the listed API snapshots; ChatGPT product availability may differ. Whether OpenAI will offer dedicated capacity after 14 January is not settled in the public notice.

stories.theme: Anthropic opens Opus 5.5 fast mode to everyone who can pay for it
stories.changed: On Wednesday 15 October 2026, Anthropic’s Claude Platform release notes said fast mode for Claude Opus 5.5 is out of research preview. You no longer need to request access or send the `fast-mode-2026-02-01` beta header. Start, Build and Scale usage tiers now get a default fast-mode rate limit. Fast mode is also available on Claude in Microsoft Foundry for deployments hosted on Azure. Anthropic’s fast-mode docs say it runs the same model weights with a faster inference setup, delivering up to 2.5 times higher output tokens per second, with the gain on streaming throughput rather than time to first token. Pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, double the standard Opus 5.5 rates of $4 and $20. Fast mode for Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 stays in research preview. It is not available on Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS or Google Cloud, and it has its own rate limits separate from standard Opus.
stories.matters: For teams that already pay for Opus on agentic coding or interactive review, the blocker was access, not a new model. Speed is now a pricing switch you can turn on in the API or with `/fast` in Claude Code, which means cost and latency become an explicit product decision rather than a waitlist.
stories.imply: Treat fast mode as a budget line, not a free upgrade. Use it where a human is waiting on the stream; keep standard speed for overnight batches.
uses: Turn on `speed: "fast"` (or `/fast` in Claude Code) only for interactive loops such as live debugging and pair-programming, and leave batch jobs on standard speed.
Add a fallback that retries without fast mode when you hit a 429 on the fast-mode limit, and log `usage.speed` so finance can see the mix.
If you run on Azure Foundry, confirm you are on Anthropic’s Azure-hosted Claude deployment; Anthropic-hosted Foundry deployments do not get fast mode.
stories.example: A platform lead at a bank keeps overnight document agents on standard Opus 5.5. For the midday incident channel, the runbook sets `speed: "fast"` and alerts if fast-mode remaining tokens fall below a floor.
stories.audience: Engineering and platform teams on Claude API or Claude Code, FinOps owners of AI spend, and Azure Foundry buyers.
stories.watch: Whether Bedrock and Google Cloud get fast mode. How often 429s force fallbacks in production. Whether Team and Enterprise Claude Code owners enable usage-credit fast mode by default.

stories.theme: Microsoft finishes pre-training MAI-Base-2 and says it will license the weights on Foundry
stories.changed: On Wednesday 15 October 2026 Microsoft AI published that it had completed pre-training MAI-Base-2, a mixture-of-experts foundation model with 80 billion active and 2.8 trillion total parameters. The company says it trained the model on 16,000 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs over 38 days in August and September 2026, with a 50 trillion-token mixture and a March 2026 knowledge cutoff. Microsoft claims MAI-Base-2 outperforms every open-weight base model it tested and is 4 to 12 times more pre-training FLOPs-efficient than DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base. Unlike MAI-Base-1, it is pre-trained natively with vision. The post stresses organic data with no distillation from other models, and says that provenance “will enable us to license our model weights to trusted partners through Foundry.” MAI-Base-2 is in post-training; preparations for MAI-Base-3 have started.
stories.matters: Microsoft is no longer only a host for OpenAI models. A Foundry path to licensed Microsoft weights is a procurement option for buyers who want a frontier stack with clearer training-data claims and Azure-native controls.
stories.imply: If you already buy models on Azure, put MAI on the shortlist beside OpenAI and Claude — but only once a post-trained product and pricing land. Do not redesign production on a base-model blog post.
uses: Ask your Microsoft account team when MAI-Base-2 post-trained variants will appear in Foundry, at what price, and under what weight-license terms.
Compare data-provenance and distillation claims in your vendor questionnaire against OpenAI and Anthropic answers you already have.
Keep a dual-vendor plan: one production model you trust today, and a measured evaluation slot for MAI once it ships.
stories.example: A cloud architect at an insurer adds “MAI-Base-2 Foundry GA date, weight-license scope, and residency” to the Q4 vendor review, and leaves the current GPT and Claude routes unchanged until those answers are written.
stories.audience: Azure and Foundry buyers, AI platform architects, vendor-risk and procurement leads.
stories.watch: Post-training results and product names. Weight-licensing terms and which partners get them. MAI-Base-3 timing and any Maia-chip co-design claims for 2027.

source.title: Microsoft AI, Frontier Pre-training at Microsoft AI
source.quote: This will enable us to license our model weights to trusted partners through Foundry, which provides enterprises with a trusted source of world-class intelligence that serves their needs.

stories.theme: Anthropic tells investors Q3 revenue hit $16.8 billion and that it was cash-flow positive
stories.changed: On 14–15 October 2026, people familiar with a pre-IPO investor meeting told CNBC that Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, up from about $11.6 billion in the second quarter and $4.7 billion in the first. The same sources said Anthropic told investors it was profitable on an adjusted basis in the third quarter. Axios, citing figures first reported by the Financial Times, said the company also claimed to be cash-flow positive, with the FT figure of $1.70 in revenue for every dollar spent on computing. CNBC and others say an IPO is reportedly slated for November. The numbers are private disclosures, not an audited public filing.
stories.matters: While public markets fretted about AI spend, Anthropic is arguing that frontier models can already clear cash. For buyers, that changes the vendor-risk question from “will this lab survive?” to “what happens to price and product when it is a public company?”
stories.imply: Expect sharper commercial terms and more disclosure pressure around Claude. Lock multi-year pricing and data-handling terms before an IPO roadshow reshapes the pitch.
uses: Update your Anthropic vendor file with the reported Q3 figures and mark them as unaudited, sourced from press accounts of an investor meeting.
Ask your account team how pricing, rate limits and enterprise commitments will change if the company lists in November.
Stress-test your Claude dependency: what breaks if list prices rise 20–30%, the premium Axios says Bloomberg Intelligence attributes to Anthropic.
stories.example: A FinOps lead renewing a Claude enterprise agreement asks for a written price collar through mid-2027 and attaches the CNBC report as the reason the collar matters now.
stories.audience: CFOs and FinOps, AI procurement, and executives whose products lean on Claude.
stories.watch: IPO filing and whether the $16.8 billion figure appears in audited statements. How OpenAI’s reported run rate and hyperscaler earnings compare. Whether premium pricing holds against open-weight competition.

source.title: CNBC, Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue is said to hit $16.8 billion ahead of IPO
source.quote: Anthropic told investors its third-quarter revenue stands at $16.8 billion as it prepares for a highly anticipated initial public offering reportedly slated for November, according to people familiar with the matter.

stories.theme: OpenAI will remove GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 from the API on 14 January 2027
stories.changed: On Tuesday 14 October 2026 OpenAI’s deprecations page said developers using certain GPT-4 series models were notified that those models leave the API on 14 January 2027. The list covers GPT-4o snapshots `gpt-4o-2024-08-06` and `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, GPT-4o mini `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, GPT-4.1 `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`, and GPT-4.1 mini `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`. Fine-tuned versions follow the same shutdown date. The recommended replacement is `gpt-6-luna`. That is about three months from notice to shutdown. On the same page OpenAI says that, unless safety or compliance require a faster timeline, generally available models get at least six months’ notice.
stories.matters: Many production apps, evals and fine-tunes still pin GPT-4o. A January cutoff with three months’ notice is a calendar risk for anyone who treated “generally available” as a six-month promise.
stories.imply: Inventory every call path that still names GPT-4o or GPT-4.1 this week. Migrate on purpose before the holiday freeze, not in the first week of January.
uses: Search code, config and prompt registries for `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4.1` and fine-tune IDs; open a migration ticket per product with a 14 January hard stop.
Run side-by-side evals of `gpt-6-luna` on your top workflows before changing the default, and keep a rollback pin until mid-January.
Ask OpenAI sales in writing whether dedicated capacity after shutdown is available for any critical fine-tune you cannot retrain in time.
stories.example: A payments product owner finds three services still on `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`. She schedules luna parity tests for the next sprint and blocks any new feature work that adds another 4o dependency.
stories.audience: Engineering leads, ML platform teams, and product owners with OpenAI API workloads.
stories.watch: Whether ChatGPT consumer access to 4o diverges from the API timeline. Dedicated-capacity offers. Behaviour diffs between luna and 4o on your eval suite.
